sub: For Women · Wide Margin · Note-Taking · 8x10 Journaling Edition

hook.h2: He spoke first, and He used her name
hook.text: "Hagar, Sarai's servant," he said, "where have you come from, and where are you going?" "I'm running away from my mistress Sarai," she replied.
father: "where have you come from, and where are you going?"
hook.note: Hagar was a servant, pregnant, running, and nobody's first concern. Our Father found her at a spring in the wilderness, opened with her name, and asked her a question instead of passing a verdict. She is the first person in Scripture to give Him a name of her own — the One who sees me — and she gave it after being heard. That is the exchange this edition is built for: His words in BLUE on the page, and two inches of blank margin beside them for yours.

short350: The world is loud with voices that arrive daily. Some of them are not kind. Some of them have named you things your Father never called you.
Father's Heart Bible is the first Bible in print where you can see who is speaking.
Our Father's words in BLUE. The Son's in RED. The Spirit's in PURPLE.

For a hundred and twenty-five years, red letters have shown the Son speaking. Our Father speaks more than three times as often — 125,457 words across 5,623 verses — and every one of them has been printed in the same black ink as the genealogies. More than one word in four of the Bible is a divine person speaking, and most of us have read past it our whole lives. The color marks ownership, not quotation: His words stay His on any lips that carry them faithfully, words He never spoke are never colored, and narration stays black.

When our Father found Hagar in the wilderness she was running, pregnant, and unwanted. He spoke first, and He called her by name. She heard Him, and named Him: the One who sees me. That is what this Bible does — not tell you about a Father who speaks, but show you where He already has.

He is not distant. He is not disappointed. He is your Heavenly Father, and He delights in you as His beloved daughter. If father is not a word of comfort for you, this Bible is especially for you: the Father revealed here is no projection of broken human fatherhood, but the original, from whom every family in heaven and on earth takes its name.

Then two inches of blank margin wait beside every page for your answer to Him. That is the whole design of this edition: the page is a conversation, and half of it is left for you. Room for a date and what He said on it, for the question you brought and where it got answered, for the line you want to be able to find again in ten years.

This is the only edition that is not 6 x 9. Eight by ten, hardcover, 788 pages, set in two columns so the text stays readable and the margin stays wide enough to actually use — full color throughout, with a presentation page that carries her name.
A fresh translation from the original Hebrew, Aramaic, and Greek — complete, 66 books and 31,085 verses. A gift, a keepsake, an heirloom.
Receive the Father. Hear His voice. His heart is for you.

body: She Hears Her Father's Voice is a wide-margin journaling Bible for women — the first Bible in print where you can see who is speaking.
Our Father's words in BLUE. The Son's words in RED. The Spirit's words in PURPLE.

For a hundred and twenty-five years, the red letter Bible has shown you the Son speaking. Our Father speaks more than three times as often — 125,457 words across 5,623 verses — and every one of them has been printed in the same black ink as the genealogies. He has been speaking the whole time. No Bible has ever shown you where.

When our Father found Hagar in the wilderness, she was running, pregnant, and unwanted. He spoke first, and He called her by name. She heard Him, and she gave Him a name no one had given Him before: the One who sees me.

The world is loud with voices that bombard you daily. Some are not kind. Some have named you things your Father never called you. His name for you is older than all of them, and in this Bible you can see exactly where He says it.
That is what this edition was made to do. Not to tell you about a Father who speaks, but to show you where He already has — and then to leave you room to answer.

long.h: Two Inches Of Margin, Beside Every Page
body: This is the wide-margin edition, and the margin is the point. Two inches of blank, unruled paper run beside every page of Scripture, at a full eight by ten inches — a larger page than the 6 x 9 editions, set in two columns, with the text where you can read it and the space where you can write.

Room for the date and what He said on it. Room for the question you brought and the verse that answered it. Room for a prayer in your own hand, a name, a note to the daughter or the friend who will open this after you.

A journaling Bible only works if the space is genuinely usable, which is why this one is 788 pages at 8 x 10 rather than a 6 x 9 with a hopeful strip down the side. It is a devotional Bible for daily Bible reading and intimacy with God, built so that hearing Him and answering Him happen on the same page.

God is our Father. Not a role He plays. Father is who He is, and Father is His name, the name Jesus came to reveal: "I revealed your name to those you gave me from the world" (John 17:6). This translation lets the Hebrew and Greek speak the distinction they always made: God as Father, Abba Father, your Heavenly Father — and you, His beloved daughter.

The color is a mark of ownership, not of quotation. His words stay His on any lips that carry them faithfully, and words He never spoke are never colored. Our Father speaks 125,457 words here. The Son speaks 39,936. More than one word in four of this Bible is a divine person speaking.

If the word father is not a word of comfort for you, this Bible is especially for you. The Father revealed here is no projection of broken human fatherhood. He is the original, from whom every family in heaven and on earth takes its name. He loved you before He created you. He sees you.

faq.q: How wide are the margins, and can I actually write in them?
faq.a: Two inches of blank, unruled paper beside every page of Scripture — enough for a dated note, a prayer, or a few lines of your own beside the verse they belong to. That is what the larger 8 x 10 page buys: the text stays readable in two columns and the margin stays genuinely usable, instead of the narrow strip you get when a 6 x 9 tries to be a journaling Bible.

faq.q: How is this different from the other fifteen editions?
faq.a: It is the only one that is not 6 x 9. This is an 8 x 10 hardcover of 788 pages, laid out in two columns with a two-inch writing margin, and it is $124.99 rather than $99.99 because of the larger trim and page. The translation inside is the same complete Father's Heart Bible™ in Divine Voice Color — 66 books, 1,189 chapters, 31,085 verses — and the opening pages are written for a woman.

faq.q: Why is it called She Hears Her Father's Voice?
faq.a: Because of Hagar. She was a servant, pregnant and running, and our Father came to her at a spring in the wilderness, spoke first, and asked her a question rather than passing a verdict. She is the first person in Scripture to give Him a name of her own — the One who sees me. The edition is named for what happened to her, and built so it can happen on your page.

It is made to be one. There is a presentation page for her name, a giver and a date, and a wide-margin Bible is one of the few gifts that gets more personal every year it is used. Order direct and shipping is free.

The color is a mark of ownership, not of quotation — His words stay His on any lips that carry them faithfully, and words He never spoke are never colored.
